module.purpose: Durable Object that drains the PostgreSQL effect outbox for file changes, dispatches file effects to room and snapshot services, retries failures, and maintains periodic liveness sweeps.
module.summary: This worker coordinates durable, ordered processing of file effects emitted into PostgreSQL. It coalesces concurrent wakeups, polls eligible outbox rows, dispatches file notifications and snapshot publication operations, records analytics, retries failures with capped exponential backoff, defers later effects for the same entity, and parks repeatedly failing rows. Cloudflare alarms provide both poke-driven execution and periodic recovery for missed triggers or restarts.
module.businessContext: Supports collaborative file synchronization by ensuring persisted file changes reach room clients and snapshot systems. Failures can delay user-visible updates, publishing, or eventually lose effects when rows are parked.

moduleContractTests.scenario: When the processor is poked, it schedules an alarm for immediate execution.
moduleContractTests.then: processor.ctx.storage.setAlarm was called with a timestamp no later than Date.now()
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pokes must start or promptly resume outbox draining.

moduleContractTests.scenario: After an alarm drain completes, the processor schedules the next sweep.
moduleContractTests.then: ctx.storage.setAlarm is called with a future timestamp
moduleContractTests.rationale: The periodic sweep must survive completed drains and runtime restarts.

moduleContractTests.scenario: When multiple drain requests overlap, only one drain operation is executed.
moduleContractTests.then: drainOutbox is called exactly once and both calls share the same promise
moduleContractTests.rationale: Coalescing prevents concurrent processing of the same outbox workload.

moduleContractTests.scenario: When an effect fails, the row is backed off and later effects for the same entity are deferred.
moduleContractTests.then: the failed row's attempts increase, nextRetryAt is set, and later same-entity rows receive a nextRetryAt no earlier than that backoff
moduleContractTests.rationale: Per-entity ordering must hold across retries.

moduleContractTests.scenario: When a supported file effect completes successfully, its outbox row is deleted.
moduleContractTests.then: effect_outbox row row.id is deleted and processed is incremented
moduleContractTests.rationale: Successful effects must not be replayed indefinitely.

moduleContractTests.scenario: When an outbox row references an unregistered source table, it is reported and not processed by a handler.
moduleContractTests.then: an exception for an unhandled table is captured and no effect handler is invoked
moduleContractTests.rationale: Unknown trigger sources must fail visibly rather than silently execute the wrong effect.

moduleContractTests.scenario: When a failure reaches the maximum attempt threshold, the failure is reported as parked.
moduleContractTests.then: outbox_parked is written with the row table name and command
moduleContractTests.rationale: Parking is the observable data-loss boundary after retries are exhausted.

postconditions: If a Sentry client is configured, its withScope callback is invoked and the exception is passed to captureException.
If extras is provided, those key-value pairs are attached to the temporary Sentry scope before captureException is invoked.
If no Sentry client is configured, no Sentry operation is performed.
invariants: The input exception is forwarded unchanged to Sentry captureException.
Scope extras are set before the exception is captured.
edgeCases: When the optional extras argument is omitted or undefined, no extras are added to the scope.
When extras is an empty object, it is still supplied to setExtras because objects are truthy.
When the Sentry client is absent, the call completes without capturing the exception.
Exceptions thrown by the configured Sentry client are not caught by this method.

raises: Any exception thrown by the configured Sentry withScope or captureException operation propagates to the caller.

detail.summary: Reports an exception to the configured Sentry client within a temporary scope. When extras are supplied, they are attached to that scope before the exception is captured; when no client is configured, the method does nothing.

postconditions: If no drain is in flight, an asynchronous _drain operation is started and tracked.
If a drain is already in flight, no additional _drain operation is started.
The tracked drain latch is cleared when the tracked drain operation settles, subject to the promise identity guard.

The in-flight drain promise is not cleared by completion of an obsolete promise after the latch has been replaced.

When called during an existing drain, the call is a no-op and coalesces with the existing operation.
When the drain operation settles, its latch is cleared only if the stored latch still refers to that operation.

detail.name: _drain
preconditions: The processor environment is configured so a PostgreSQL connection pool and file effect dependencies can be created.
The effect outbox schema and the file effect handler are available.
postconditions: Eligible outbox rows are processed in ascending id order through the outbox drain mechanism.
Successfully processed rows are deleted and counted as processed.
Failed rows have their attempts and retry scheduling updated, and later same-entity rows are deferred to preserve ordering.
Rows that have reached the parking threshold are eligible for deletion by the configured parked-row cleanup.
invariants: Only rows with attempts below MAX_ATTEMPTS and with no retry time or a retry time at or before the current database time are selected.
At most 50 rows are selected per batch.
Rows are selected in ascending outbox id order.
A failed row's later siblings with the same tableName and entityId are not scheduled earlier than the failed row's backoff.
Deferring later siblings does not increment their attempt counts.
Backoff is exponential from the row's current attempt count and is capped at 300 seconds.
edgeCases: An outbox row whose tableName has no registered handler is reported to captureException and dropped without invoking an effect handler.
A handler failure increments the failed count, updates the failed row's attempt count and retry time, and defers later same-entity siblings.
A failure that reaches the parking threshold is treated as a parking failure for reporting purposes.
Rows whose attempts are at least MAX_ATTEMPTS are excluded from normal batch selection and are handled by parked-row cleanup according to its age threshold.
A publish failure is passed to captureException with publishThumbnailEnqueue set to true by the publish dependency.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Unhandled table names are reported and dropped; effect-handler failures are passed to the outbox drain error path for retry and possible parking.
